## TL;DR

Completed a focused QA pass of the review and Move to done drawer flow. The existing implementation and fixture suite cover the requested workflow states, and the responsive rules address the main phone hazards: narrow drawer sizing, reachable tabs, wrapping action rows, and touch-sized controls. I found no actionable UI defect during this pass, so the change records the QA coverage and its limits rather than changing working behavior.

## Work and rationale

I read the task specification from this worktree and traced the review and close-out path through `TaskDrawer.vue`, its shared styles, the preview fixture registry, and the task-drawer tests. The task asks for state-based QA across phone, tablet, and desktop widths, with special attention to failure states and button reachability.

The fixture inventory already has distinct examples for a review task with a blocked landing checklist (`drawer:landable` and its narrow variant), review failure, handoff failure, running close-out stages, a close-out error (`card:doneError`), and a landed post-merge summary. Needs-input coverage is represented by the human-step and held fixtures, while component tests pin the critical banner placement and failure wording. I recorded the relevant state/test mapping and responsive observations in `docs/qa/2026-11-review-flow-qa.md` so future work can see what this pass actually covered.

The responsive source review focused on the interactions with the highest risk at phone width. Below 720 px the drawer fills the viewport, the header controls are ordered to preserve back and close access, the tab strip wraps so tabs do not disappear offscreen, and touch targets are given a 44 px minimum. The shared drawer body remains vertically scrollable and clips horizontal overflow. At tablet width the drawer remains a panel and the action rows can wrap; desktop retains the resizable panel behavior. The landing checklist's body copy and next steps are allowed to wrap. A headless WebKit smoke run passed and exercised the task drawer at 360 px, but it did not measure the requested state-by-width matrix at 375, 768, and 1280 px.

## Approaches tried

I first located the task file and fixture/test surface. The path in the task pack had a shortened filename, so I used `rg --files work` within the authorized worktree to locate the actual task file. I then cross-checked the fixtures against `TaskDrawer.vue` and existing tests, including assertions for landing submission, needs-input visibility, failed close-out details, and status summaries.

I chose not to alter UI logic or CSS because the existing behavior and coverage showed no concrete defect. The new QA note distinguishes fixture-backed states from limitations. The focused suite passed 27 tests; `bun run build` and the headless `bun run smoke` passed. The requested scoped check also passed; because final changed paths were documentation-only, RepoOS skipped build, full tests, and UI smoke in that run.

## Challenges and blockers

No blocker prevented completing the source and documentation review. This worktree is the only checkout used. The main checkout was not read or modified, and `repoos.toml` was left untouched. The smoke run checked the drawer at 360 px, but did not cover every requested fixture at every requested width; no physical phone or tablet was available. The QA note states those limits.

## Key learnings

The drawer already has useful state fixtures, including narrow variants for selected states, but they are distributed between the general preview fixture module and focused component tests. The most reliable QA record is therefore a map linking each user-visible phase to both its preview state and its behavioral assertion. Phone layout is intentionally a full-screen task detail with wrapped tabs, while 768 px keeps the side-panel model; those distinct breakpoints should both remain part of future drawer changes.
